newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-minister faces October war crimes trial.
newsitem.headline: French ex-minister faces October war crimes trial.

text.p: The trial of French former cabinet minister Maurice Papon for crimes against humanity is likely to take place in October if work on the courtroom is completed in time, justice officials said on Wednesday.
In a statement, the court in the southwestern town of Bordeaux endorsed the month of October as suggested by civil plaintiffs in the trial over the deportation of 1,560 Jews to Nazi death camps.
Bordeaux plans to build a special courtroom for Papon's trial, which is expected to last several weeks.
The Supreme Court last month ordered Papon, 86, to face an assize court for his wartime activities, quashing his last-ditch attempt to avoid trial after 16 years of legal wrangling.
Papon was secretary-general of the southwestern Bordeaux region under German occupation during World War Two.
He enjoyed a brilliant post-war career as Paris police chief from 1968 to 1974 and budget minister in the 1970s before his wartime record became known.
He denies the charges and says he remained at his job on orders of the Resistance.
